IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION 
CRIMINAL APPEAL  NO.2342 OF 2010
SANTOSH A. BEHERE                                   APPELLANT(S)
                                VERSUS
THE STATE OF MAHARASHTRA                               RESPONDENT(S)
WITH
CRIMINAL APPEAL  NO.1736 OF 2011
RAHUL RAGHUNATH DANDGE                            APPELLANT(S)
                                VERSUS
THE STATE OF MAHARASHTRA                                    RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
The  present  appeals  have  been  filed  challenging  the  common
impugned judgment and order dated 16 th April, 2009 passed by the High
Court  of  Judicature  at  Bombay  in  Criminal  Appeal  No.1263  of  2002,
whereby the conviction of the appellants under Sections 143, 147, 148,
302 read with Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code, 18601 was upheld. 
2. Though none is present for the appellant-Santosh A. Behere, yet as the
two appeals arise from a common impugned judgment, this Court, with the
1  For short the ‘IPC’
1

--- Page 546 ---
assistance of learned counsel for the parties, has heard arguments in appeal
No.1736 of 2011 filed by the co-accused Rahul Raghunath Dandge and
perused  the  common  impugned  judgment  as  well  as  the  Trial  Court
records.
3. At the outset, learned counsel for the appellant – Rahul Raghunath
Dandge states that the appellants in the aforesaid criminal appeals have
suffered incarceration for more than 15 years without remission.
4. Copies of custody certificates handed over by learned counsel for the
respondent-State of Maharashtra are taken on record.
5. A  perusal  of  the  eye-witness  statements  of  PW1  (complainant–
Basappa) and PW8(Jagdish Shetty) proves that the appellants and other
co-convicts had come together armed with the intent to cause death or
injuries to the deceased, which were likely to cause death. The appellants -
Santosh  A.  Behere  and  Rahul  Raghunath  Dandge  have  been  ascribed
specific role of assaulting the deceased with the handle of a spade and a
sword  respectively.  The  relevant  portion  of  the  evidence  of  PW1
(complainant–Basappa) is reproduced hereinbelow:
“….At that time, Rahul Dandge beat me with a handle of spade on my
back. Suresh Chavan was holding gupti in his hand.……….Thereafter, I
accompanied the police to show them houses of the accused persons and
on our way we saw that the accused persons were beating Tanaji Pawar
near his house. On seeing the police, the accused persons ran away.
Tanaji Pawar was lying in an injured condition. He was having stab
injuries on his chest which Suresh Chavan caused him by assaulting him
with gupti. Tanaji Pawar was having other injuries also. Santosh Behere
was holding handle of spade while so assaulting Tanaji. Rahul Dandge
was holding sword while so assaulting Tanaji Pawar.”
2

--- Page 547 ---
6. It  is  settled  law  that  for  application  of  Section  149  IPC,  the
prosecution is required to prove the following:
i. There must be an unlawful assembly.
ii. Commission of an offence by any member of an unlawful
assembly 
iii. Such offence must have been committed in prosecution of
the  common  object  of  the  assembly,  or  must  be  such  as  the
members of the assembly knew to be likely to be committed2. 
7. It is also settled law that mere presence in the unlawful assembly may
fasten vicariously criminal liability under Section 149 IPC. Furthermore,
in case of unlawful assembly, if proof of common object is furnished, then
conviction with the help of Section 149 IPC is permissible. 
8. In the present  case,  not only have the appellants been ascribed  the
specific role in the death of the deceased, but the evidence on record also
shows that the appellants along with other co-convicts were armed and
assembled  together  in  search  of  the  deceased.  Therefore,  there  was  a
common object and each member of the unlawful assembly, including the
appellants, were aware that they had the common object of attacking the
deceased with various weapons, which may cause or likely to cause death.
2   Gurmail Singh Vs. State of Punjab [(2013) 4 SCC 228]
3

--- Page 548 ---
9. Consequently, this Court is of the view that, on merits, the impugned
judgment does not warrant any interference. 
10. However, on the quantum of sentence, this Court is of the view that as
the appellants have undergone incarceration for more than 15 years, their
sentence should be reduced to the period undergone. Ordered accordingly. 
11. With  the  aforesaid  directions,  the  present  Criminal  Appeals  stand
disposed of along with pending application(s), if any.

      IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
 CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO(S).     of 2026
(@PETITION FOR SPECIAL LEAVE TO APPEAL (C) NO.22433/2024)
SUBHA & ORS.                                       …APPELLANT(S)
                                VERSUS
THE UNITED INDIA INSURANCE COMPANY LTD. & ORS.     …RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. Present appeal has been filed challenging the final judgment
and order dated 24th March 2023 passed by the Madurai Bench of the
High Court of Madras in CMA(MD) No.288 of 2023 whereby the High
Court  has  considered  the  net  income  of  the  deceased  for
determining the quantum of compensation under the head ‘Loss of
Income’.
3. Learned counsel for the Appellants submits that the High
Court erred in holding that the net income of the deceased has to
be considered for determining the quantum of compensation under
the head ‘Loss of Income’. According to him, this approach is in
direct contravention of the well-established principle of law
laid down by this Court which mandates consideration of gross
income for such calculation. He submits that this deviation from
the settled principle of law has resulted in reduction of the
compensation  amount  due  and  payable  to  the  Appellants  from
Rs.42,63,904/- to Rs.27,97,000/-.
Page   1 of  1

--- Page 574 ---
4. Learned counsel for the Appellants further submits that the
High Court erroneously placed reliance upon the judgment of this
Court in  National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi &
Ors., (2017) 16 SCC 680  to hold that net income ought to be
considered for calculating the compensation payable under the head
‘Loss of Income’.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for Respondent-Insurance company
submits  that  the  High  Court  has  correctly  calculated  the
compensation amount under the head ‘Loss of Income’ in accordance
with judgment in National Insurance Company Limited (supra) on the
basis of gross income of the deceased. He further submits that the
Respondent-Insurance company has already complied with the impugned
High Court judgment and has deposited the entire compensation
amount with the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kuzhithurai.
6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties, this Court finds
that the issue whether compensation under the head ‘Loss of Income’
is to be calculated on the basis of gross income or net income has
been conclusively settled by this Court in Kalpanaraj & Ors. vs.
Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation, (2015) 2 SCC 764 wherein it
has been held as under:-
“9. In the light of the principle of law laid down by this Court
in the Indira Srivastava case [National Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Indira Srivastava, (2008) 2 SCC 763] mentioned supra, we are of
the opinion that the High Court erred in making deductions under
various  heads  to  arrive  at  the  net  income  instead  of
ascertaining the gross income of the deceased out of the annual
income earned from his occupation mentioned in the income tax
return submitted for the relevant Financial Year 1994-1995.”
Page   2 of  2

--- Page 575 ---
7. In view of the aforesaid categorical exposition of law, the
impugned judgment of the High Court is set aside and the order
dated  25th March,  2022  passed  by  the  Motor  Accidents  Claims
Tribunal, Kuzhithurai in MCOP No. 22 of 2016, is restored. The
Respondent-Insurance Company is directed to pay the compensation
amount in accordance with the order passed by the Motor Accidents
Claims Tribunal, Kuzhithurai, to the Appellants within eight weeks
from today.
8. Accordingly, present appeal is disposed of. There is no order
as to costs.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.  
  ………………………………………………………. J.
                 [R.MAHADEVAN]
……………………………………………………...J.
                 [MANMOHAN]
NEW DELHI;
JULY 27, 2026.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioners are family members/close relatives of certain
Indian nationals belonging to the States of Rajasthan, Punjab,
Haryana, and Himachal Pradesh, who are stated to have travelled to
the  Russian  Federation  between  2024  and  2025,  on  different
categories of visas. It is alleged that most of them were duped by
travel agents with the promise of employment opportunities in the
1

--- Page 578 ---
construction, hospitality, and service sectors. However, upon their
arrival in Russia, their passports and identity documents were
confiscated, and they were enrolled in the Russian Armed Forces,
and were consequently taken to the line of fire in the ongoing
Russia-Ukraine armed conflict. Unfortunately, many young Indian
citizens have lost their lives in the ongoing hostilities, but
their mortal remains have not been brought back to India after due
verification. Similarly, it is submitted that no compensation
amount has been paid to the bereaved families.
2. The instant matter has been heard on several occasions, and
most recently, the Union of India has filed an additional status
report.
3. Taking into consideration the prevailing circumstances and
relevant factors, and with a view to resolve the pending issues, we
deem it appropriate to issue the following directions at this
juncture:
(i) The Ministry of External Affairs shall notify an officer
as the Nodal Officer, whose relevant particulars and
contact number shall be provided to the family members of
the deceased/injured Indian nationals who had gone to
Russia.
(ii) In the event of a fatality/casualty, the Ministry of
External Affairs will arrange DNA tests of the mortal
remains with the family members for the identification of
the deceased body, and upon doing such an exercise, the
deceased body along with a certificate of the DNA test
shall be handed over to the concerned family.
2

--- Page 579 ---
(iii) A complete set of the consolidated documents regarding
the procedure to file for attaining compensation, which
is  to  be  filed  with  the  Russian  authorities,  duly
translated  in  regional  language  along  with  other
necessary documents, may be supplied to the affected
families. Such families may submit their claims with the
Russian authorities through the Ministry of External
Affairs. However, pendency of such claims should not be a
ground to delay the cremation, performing other rituals,
or the handing over of the mortal remains, which should
all be separately expedited.
(iv) The District Legal Services Authorities of the States of
Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh through
their Member Secretaries, are directed to provide free
legal aid to the aggrieved families for the purpose of
submission of claims and/or conducting of DNA test, apart
from  other  necessary  legal/administrative  formalities
which are required to be completed by them.
4. The  Ministry  of  External  Affairs  may  also  supply  the
translated  version  of  the  documents  received  from  Russian
authorities, if not already done so, having relevance to the return
of the mortal remains or with respect to the compensation claims.
5. We lastly direct the Ministry of External Affairs, Government
of India, to continue its efforts to bring back the remaining
deceased bodies/mortal remains and/or trace the missing persons
3

--- Page 580 ---
through the relevant diplomatic channels.
6. Post the matter on for further consideration on 31.08.2026.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.   3571   OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL) NO. 11567/2026)
GURPREET      APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
STATE OF HARYANA       RESPONDENT(S)
ORDER
1. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and
learned counsel for the respondent-State of Haryana.
2. Leave granted.
3. This  appeal  takes  exception  to  the  order  dated
06.03.2026 passed by the High court of Punjab and Haryana
(briefly the ‘High Court’ hereinafter), rejecting the
prayer for anticipatory bail of the appellant.
4. It is stated that appellant has been arrayed as an
accused in FIR No.154/2025 registered at Police Station-
Cyber  Crime,  District-  Rewari,  Haryana  under  Section
318(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (for short,
‘BNS’)
5. Allegation against the appellant is that he had
cheated the informant of a substantial sum of money by
posing as a Stock Broker investing in shares.
6. This Court, by order dated 15.06.2026, had issued
notice and granted interim protection to the appellant
subject  to  the  appellant  co-operating  with  the
1

--- Page 609 ---
investigation.
7. Learned  counsel  for  the  appellant  submits  that
appellant has been roped in on the basis of a disclosure
statement made by a co-accused. Pursuant to order dated
15.06.2026 passed by this Court, appellant has joined
investigation.
8. This fact is not disputed by learned counsel for the
respondent-State of Haryana.
9. Considering the above, we are of the view that the
interim protection granted by this Court vide order dated
15.06.2026 should be made absolute.
10. That being the position, we set aside the impugned
order dated 06.03.2026 passed by the High Court and make
the  order  dated  15.06.2026  absolute.  However,  the
appellant  shall  continue  to  co-operate  with  the
investigation of the case.
11. Consequently, the Criminal Appeal is allowed.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

1. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned
Additional Advocate General appearing for the State. 
2. The  present  petition  calls  in  question  the
correctness  of  the  order  dated  17-04-2026  in

--- Page 621 ---
2
S.B.Criminal  Miscellaneous  Second  Bail  Application
No.4910/2026 passed by the High Court of Judicature for
Rajasthan at Jaipur. By the said order, the petitioner
has been denied the benefit of bail in connection with
FIR No.133/2025 registered with Arain Police Station,
District Ajmer, Rajasthan, for the offences punishable
under  Sections  8/15  o f  the  Narcotic  Drugs  and
Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (for short, ‘NDPS’).
3. When the matter came up on 01.06.2026, this Court
sought for a series of particulars from the State’s
counsel.  The  State  has  also  filed  the  counter
affidavit, which we have perused.
4. The allegation against the petitioner is that he was
the owner of the vehicle from which the contraband was
seized. Admittedly, the petitioner was not in the
vehicle at the time of the seizure. The case of the
petitioner is that the vehicle had been taken on hire
and that he has not involved in the offence.
5. In any event, these are matters for trial. The
petitioner has already undergone about 11 months in
custody. Out of 24 witnesses which are listed, as at
present 03 witnesses have been examined; the trial is
likely to take some time to conclude.
6. Keeping  the  nature  of  allegation  against  the
petitioner;  the  period  already  undergone  by  the
petitioner; the time that the trial is likely to take
and keeping in mind the twin condition of Section 37 of

--- Page 622 ---
3
the NDPS Act, we are inclined to enlarge the petitioner
on bail.
7. Accordingly, we direct that petitioner shall be
enlarged on bail subject to the satisfaction of the
concerned Trial Court in connection with the aforesaid
FIR and for the offences mentioned hereinabove.
8. The Special Leave Petition is disposed of in the
above terms.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand
disposed of.

made available by the Respondent with limitation that on

the  Corporate  Insolvency  Resolution  Process,  the
2

of RSIL for verification. FAR records that no specific
evidence was found indicating diversion or siphoning of

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Civil Appeal No.10232/2016
N. M. SHANOJ                     APPELLANT
VERSUS
STATE OF KERALA . & ORS.                   RESPONDENTS
O R D E R
1. Leave was granted by this Court on the appellant’s special leave petition 1
on 07th October, 2016 referring to a special leave petition 2 titled Babu P .V. Vs.
State of Kerala and Ors. , in respect whereof leave was granted on 18 th April,
2016. The civil appeal 3 of Babu P .V. (supra) has been dismissed by us by an
order dated 22nd July, 2026.
2. We have heard Ms. Bindu A., learned counsel for the appellant as well as
Mr.  Vipin  Nair,  learned  counsel  for  the  respondent  –  Kerala  Public  Service
Commission4.
3. Within the validity period of the rank list, 10 candidates in order of merit
were  recommended  for  appointment  from  the  category  of  persons  with
disabilities. Rank of the appellant was no. 17 (seventeen).
4. Since no vacancy was available for recommending him within the validity
period of the rank list, he was not favoured with any such recommendation. 
1 Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.31011/2016
2 Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.8357/2016
3 Civil Appeal No.4096/2016
4 Commission
1

--- Page 627 ---
5. Be  that  as  it  may,  for  filling  up  posts  where  vacancies  occurred
subsequently, a special  recruitment  drive  was  initiated by the  Commission.
Despite the appellant being eligible to apply, he did not offer his candidature
and, therefore, missed the opportunity of being considered even in course of
such special recruitment drive. 
6. Our sympathies are with the appellant, who happens to be a physically
challenged candidate, but we are disabled from granting him any relief having
regard to the fact that there were others ahead of the appellant in the rank list,
who have not been recommended for appointment.
7. The civil appeal is, accordingly, dismissed.
8. Pending application(s), if any, stand disposed of.

(DIPANKAR DATTA)

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO(S).1256-1257/2019
T. VENKATESHWAR RAO(D) BY LR.                 APPELLANT(s)
                                VERSUS
L. KUMAR GOUD & ORS.                          RESPONDENT(s)
O R D E R
1. These appeals arise from the judgment and order passed
by the High Court of Judicature, Andhra Pradesh dated
23.10.2009 in Appeal Suit No.178/1994 and cross objections.
2. The appellant before us is the original plaintiff.
Suit for specific performance of contract was instituted.
The suit came to be partly decreed. 
3. The original defendants preferred First Appeal against
the judgment and order decree of specific performance and
insofar as the relief which was not granted by the Trial
Court,  cross  objections  were  filed  by  the  original
plaintiff, i.e., the appellant before us.
4. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the
appellant-original plaintiff and having gone through the
materials on record, we are of the view that no error, not
to speak of any error of law could be said to have been
committed by the Court below.
5. We are informed by the learned counsel appearing for
the appellant-plaintiff that her client has deposited the
balance sale consideration in terms of the decree of the
1

--- Page 678 ---
Trial Court. That particular amount shall be refunded to
the original plaintiff with interest, if accrued, any.
6. The original plaintiff/ legal representative(s) shall
be entitled to prefer an appropriate application before the
Trial Court for disbursement of the amount which was
deposited by them at the relevant point of time with
interest, if accrued, any.
7. With the aforesaid, the appeals are, accordingly,
dismissed.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.
…………………………………………….J.
[J.B. PARDIWALA]
…………………………………………….J.
[K. VINOD CHANDRAN]
NEW DELHI;
30th JULY, 2026

ITEM NO.5               COURT NO.10               SECTION II-B
               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL) Diary No(s). 34692/2026
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated  17-04-2026
in CRMM No. 19477/2026 passed by the High Court of Punjab & Haryana
at Chandigarh]
NIRBHAI SINGH                                      Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
STATE OF PUNJAB                                    Respondent(s)
IA No. 206742/2026 - CONDONATION OF DELAY IN REFILING /  CURING THE
DEFECTS
IA No. 206739/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF THE IMPUGNED 
JUDGMENT
IA No. 206741/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.
 
Date : 03-08-2026 This matter was called for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE AHSANUDDIN AMANULLAH
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANMOHAN 
For Petitioner(s) :Mr. Karan Dewan, Adv.
                   Ms. Aanchal Jain, AOR
                   
                   
For Respondent(s) :Ms. Baani Khanna, AOR
                   Mr. Robin Singh, Adv.
                   Mr. Kapil Balwani, Adv.
                   Ms. Komal Thakkar, Adv.
                   
                   
                             O R D E R
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel
for the respondent-State of Punjab, who has appeared on advance
notice.
2. Delay condoned.
3. With the consent of the parties, the matter has been heard on

--- Page 699 ---
2
merits.
4. The petitioner seeks bail in connection with FIR bearing No.
38 dated 07.03.2025 for the offences punishable under Sections 406,
420, 120-B IPC (Corresponding Sections 316(2), 318(4), 61(2) of
BNS, 2023) registered at P.S. Sadar Dhuri, Sangrur, Punjab.
5. Basically, the allegation against the petitioner is that he
arranged for the marriage of the complainant's son with a girl who
had cleared IELTS, so that the son of the complainant could be sent
abroad on a work permit.
6. That having failed, besides the bride side, the petitioner has
also been made an accused.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that at best, the
role of the petitioner could be that of a person who had introduced
the parties. After that, not even a single rupee has come into his
account to sustain the charge of any wrongdoing, much less criminal
conduct. It was further submitted that the petitioner in the
present case which is triable by a Magistrate, is in custody for
over seven and a half months.
8. Learned counsel for the State of Punjab submits that the
petitioner  has  two  other  antecedents  and  one  under  similar
circumstances.
9. However, it was not controverted that the money trail does not
indicate that there was any transaction between the petitioner and
the complainant.

1. The present petition has been filed for transfer of
matrimonial dispute i.e. Petition No. 937 of 2025, titled as
“Sh. Ankit Mittal vs. Saumya Gupta” , pending before the
Family Court, Sonipat, Haryana to the Family Court, Lucknow,

2. In  the  present  case,  the  matter  was  referred  for
mediation,  however,  report  has  been  received  that  the
mediation is unsuccessful.
3. The record of the case reveals that as many as 08 cases
are pending at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh and therefore, as the
respondent is attending those cases and he is also living in
Lucknow, this Court is of the opinion that the present
transfer petition deserves to be allowed.

the transfer of Petition No. 937 of 2025, titled as  “Sh.
Ankit Mittal vs. Saumya Gupta” , pending before the Family
Court, Sonipat, Haryana to the Family Court, Lucknow, Uttar

Pradesh.
